definition.en-US: A URL is the text address that says where a resource such as a web page or an image can be found on the internet.

analogy.en-US: It is like a full postal address written on one line, with the country, city, street and house number all in order.

definition.en-US: HTTPS is the encrypted form of HTTP, which protects everything that passes between your browser and the server.

analogy.en-US: It is like sending a letter in a sealed envelope that only the person it is addressed to can open.

definition.en-US: A request is the message a browser sends to a server to ask for a page or a file, and the server answers it with a response.

analogy.en-US: It is like asking the librarian at a desk for a book and waiting while they fetch it for you.

definition.en-US: A domain name is a website's address on the internet, made of labels separated by dots, such as example.com.

analogy.en-US: It is like the name on a shop front that people use to find the shop, while the street address is hidden behind it.

definition.en-US: DNS, the Domain Name System, translates a domain name into the numeric address of the server that holds the site.

analogy.en-US: It is like a phone book that turns a person's name into the number you need to call.

definition.en-US: A CDN, or content delivery network, is a group of servers in many places that keep copies of the same files so that each visitor gets a nearby copy.

analogy.en-US: It is like a chain of shops that stock the same products in every city, so you buy from the one closest to you.

definition.en-US: A static site is a website made of files that the browser receives exactly as they are, without a program that builds each page when someone asks for it.

analogy.en-US: It is like a printed brochure, where every copy says the same thing until someone prints a new edition.

definition.en-US: A build is the step that turns source files, such as templates and notes, into the final files a browser can read.

analogy.en-US: It is like baking a cake from a recipe, where the recipe is your source and the cake is what you serve.

definition.en-US: To push means to send your saved commits from your computer to the copy of the repository on GitHub.

analogy.en-US: It is like mailing a finished chapter to the publisher so that it can be printed.

definition.en-US: A workflow is a file of steps that GitHub Actions runs automatically when a chosen event happens in a repository.

analogy.en-US: It is like a recipe card that a kitchen robot follows each time a new order arrives.

definition.en-US: A run is one execution of a workflow, which shows a status and a log for each job and each step.

analogy.en-US: It is like one rehearsal of a play, with notes on every scene so you can see where it went wrong.

definition.en-US: A log is the written record of what a run or a program printed, step by step, including any error text.

analogy.en-US: It is like the flight recorder on an aeroplane, which writes down each event in the order it happened.

definition.en-US: A cache is a stored copy of a response that a browser or a service reuses instead of asking the server again.

analogy.en-US: It is like a photocopy of a menu kept at your table, which can be out of date once the restaurant changes it.

definition.en-US: A 404 Not Found response means the server cannot find the file at the address that was requested.

analogy.en-US: It is like a letter that comes back to the sender because no house with that number exists on the street.

definition.en-US: A branch is a separate line of saved changes inside a repository, so work on one branch does not change another until you combine them.

analogy.en-US: It is like a sheet of tracing paper laid over a drawing, where you sketch changes that stay separate until you copy them across.

definition.en-US: To deploy means to put finished files where the public address can serve them to visitors.

analogy.en-US: It is like hanging a finished painting in the gallery window so that passers-by can see it.

definition.en-US: A preview deployment is a test copy of a branch's changes at its own address, which does not replace the live site.

analogy.en-US: It is like a dress rehearsal on a separate stage before the show opens to the public.

definition.en-US: A rollback makes an earlier production version of a site live again.

analogy.en-US: It is like turning back to the last page you saved in a notebook before a messy edit.

definition.en-US: An edge node is a server placed near visitors that answers their requests with copies of the site it has stored.

analogy.en-US: It is like a branch library in your neighbourhood that keeps the books you borrow most often.

definition.en-US: An access key is a credential, made of an ID and a secret, that lets a program act for a cloud account, so it must stay private.

analogy.en-US: It is like a spare house key, because anyone who holds it can walk in, so you keep it somewhere safe.

definition.en-US: An ICP filing is a registration with the Chinese authorities that a domain must complete before some acceleration regions in mainland China can serve it.

analogy.en-US: It is like registering a shop with the city office before you open it to walk-in customers.

definition.en-US: An HTTPS certificate is a document issued for a domain that lets browsers confirm the site is genuine and set up an encrypted connection.

analogy.en-US: It is like an official identity card that shows the person in front of you is who they say they are.

definition.en-US: A DNS record is one entry in the naming system that says where a domain name or a subdomain should point, such as an A record or a CNAME record.

analogy.en-US: It is like one line in the phone book that says which number to call for a given name.
